n.quote: Replication results: As in the original study, the hypothesis that high economic inequality (as compared to low economic inequality) reduces the generosity of high-income individuals (as compared to low-income individuals) was tested using an ordinary least squares regression, focusing on the interaction effect of the high inequality treatment indicator and participants’ income. The interaction effect (b = 0.002, se = 0.008) turned out to be statistically insignificant: t(3649) = 0.201, p = 0.841; n = 3653. As a result, we cannot reject the null hypothesis of no interaction effect of economic inequality income. The standardized effect size (Cohen’s d) is d = –0.013 (95% CI [–0.143, 0.116]).

es.quote: The standardized effect size (Cohen’s d) is d = –0.013 (95% CI [–0.143, 0.116]).

reported_success.quote: Discussion: Given the criteria and procedure outlined above, the hypothesis of interest has not been replicated at a significance level of p < 0.05.

notes: Original and replication evaluated separately. Replication statistics are as printed in the primary authors’ post-replication report.
